affected_boundaries: native history response and terminal notification ordering

observed_behavior: Closing the adapter refused with a tracked active turn even after its terminal notification and successful terminal observation.
expected_behavior: A stale in-progress history snapshot cannot reactivate the same turn after an observed terminal transition.
causal_mechanism: The response promise resolves, a terminal notification is processed in the same input chunk, then the history response continuation calls observeNativeTurn with its earlier in-progress snapshot and restores activeTurns. waitForTurn returns the cached completion without removing that restored activity.

anti_pattern.structural_description: An asynchronous snapshot unconditionally overwrites later lifecycle evidence for the same identity.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Promise continuation order differs from the order in which the underlying server state was observed.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Observed terminal state supersedes an earlier in-progress snapshot for the identical turn.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Before tracking an in-progress history result, return an already observed terminal result for the same turn identity. Preserve active tracking for a different turn and preserve the shutdown ownership gate.

applicability_conditions: A terminal notification is processed before the continuation for a prior in-progress history response.
known_non_matches: Unknown active thread ownership has not been observed idle.
confirmation_evidence: The deterministic fixture sends a stale history response and terminal notification in one chunk. Before repair, close rejects with unresolved activity for turn-1; after repair, the history read returns completed and close succeeds.
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-codex.test.ts: terminal notifications supersede an earlier in-progress history response
